name: Fair Isaac Corporation
sector: Financial data & analytics / credit scoring and decision software
moat_justification: Measured economics are wide-moat: ROIC proxy rose 27.0% (FY20) to 63.9% (FY25), gross margin 72.1% to 82.2%, and per-score pricing power was proven over decades. But the richest pillar — the GSE mortgage mandate — was a regulation, and FHFA dismantled it in Sept 2026 (VantageScore 4.0 on one pricing grid, fees aligned); the bureaus that distribute FICO own the rival. Non-mortgage ubiquity, workflow integration and the software platform keep it a real moat, scored 6 until the post-change cycle proves what survives.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 13 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 2.3%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 5.5x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 3.4x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (7.0%) vs bull-case tier C (12.5%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Elite scoring franchise, moat 6/10 with the mortgage pillar cracked by FHFA — even on peak pre-change TTM OE of $35.01/sh, weighted IRR is only 9.3% at $771.19 (weighted IV@15% $395.24); clears the 15% hurdle only below ~$395.
moat_for: FICO Score is the embedded standard across auto, card, personal-loan and mortgage underwriting; lender models, securitization and investor reporting are built around it
Proven pricing power: repeated per-score price increases with no volume loss through FY2026 (mortgage origination revenue +97% YoY in Q3 FY26 on low-single-digit volumes)
Exceptional returns on capital: ROIC proxy 27.0% (FY20) rising to 63.9% (FY25), gross margin 82.2%, near-zero capex — asset-light royalty economics
Software platform diversifying the base: Platform ARR +62% to $413M in Q3 FY26, 51% of total ARR of $816M
moat_against: Mortgage monopoly was regulatory, not structural: FHFA put VantageScore 4.0 on the same pricing grid (Sept 29-30, 2026) and Rocket Mortgage made it the default for eligible loans from Q4 2026; FICO Score 10T is not yet eligible for loan delivery
Distribution conflict: the three bureaus that distribute FICO scores jointly own VantageScore and price it far below FICO ($4.50/score held through 2027 vs FICO's $10 per-score option)
Mortgage concentration: mortgage originations were 62% of Scores revenue in Q3 FY26, and Scores growth is price-led, not volume-led — exactly the leg now contested
Leverage rising into the fight: total debt up to $5.58B by June 2026 (from $3.06B at FY25) after $3.1B of buybacks in 9M FY26, 4.0x operating cash flow
Software ex-platform is shrinking: Software revenue +2% in Q3 FY26, non-platform ARR -17% — the offset engine is not yet big enough
